resale_co.name: Title Transfer inspection (Title Transfer Application)
resale_co.issued_by: Seaside Heights Code Enforcement / Housing Department
requirements: Visual inspection only; it does not include plumbing, heating or electrical inspections
10-year sealed lithium battery smoke detectors in each room, including the utility room and attic (not in kitchens or bathrooms)
Carbon monoxide detector where the property has gas service, mounted between sleeping areas

In pre-existing homes, a mounted 1A:10B-C 5 lb fire extinguisher in the kitchen, 4 feet from the floor and within 10 feet of the stove (Borough form dated 10/2020; state law P.L.2025, c.19 later removed the extinguisher from the state requirement)
The office checks for outstanding construction permits and whether the home was substantially damaged
Final readings on all utility bills before closing

fees.label: Title Transfer inspection, per residential unit, per inspection (check, money order or cash)
fees.quote: FEE: $100 per Residential unit/ $200 per Commercial unit, per inspection, check, money order or cash

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Title Transfer Application (owner, property, block and lot, agent, buyer, sale price, email) and submit it with the $100 per unit fee, payable to the Borough of Seaside Heights (check, money order or cash), to the Code Enforcement / Housing office, 100 Grant Avenue, Municipal Complex Building B. After the application and payment are received, an inspector contacts you to set an inspection time (inspections Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday). General questions: housing@seaside-heightsnj.org, 732-793-9100.
resale_co.contact_title: Code Enforcement, Zoning Officer & Flood Plain Manager

resale_co.notes: The Title Transfer Application is linked from the Borough's Code Enforcement/Housing page; the form code 'MN10/2020' suggests it dates from October 2020, so the $100 fee is from that form. The form cites Chapter 55 of the Borough code (ecode360 SE1678 could not be opened). A buyer who plans to rent must get a mercantile license and a rental certificate of occupancy from Code Enforcement; the Borough also runs rental and short-term rental (STRP) programs, which are rental-only. Other Code Enforcement staff on the page: Ann Phillips (Ext. 117), Jim Bonney (Ext. 197), Frank Tortoriello (Ext. 131). Office hours Monday and Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; inspections Tuesday to Thursday.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA is the fire code enforcing agency for Seaside Heights (registry code S), but the DCA's list of State-enforced towns (revised 7/17/2026) shows Seaside Heights without the 'SC' (Smoke Certs) mark, and the DCA directory (survey 1/22/2026) lists 'Seaside Heights' with the Borough Hall phone (732) 793-9100 under smoke detector compliance. The Borough's Title Transfer form certifies smoke alarms, CO alarm and extinguisher, so the Title Transfer inspection serves as the smoke/CO certificate (medium confidence). The 2020 form still lists the fire extinguisher and does not mention the 2025 secondary power source label. The Borough's rental CO guidelines ask for a 5 lb ABC extinguisher. The Seaside Heights Volunteer Fire Department (Chief Tim Farrell on the Borough page; the DCA directory says Dennis Farrell) is the fire department, not the certificate office.
